enhanced_information: In the management of hyperthyroidism during the first trimester of pregnancy, Propylthiouracil (PTU) is the preferred treatment due to its lower risk of teratogenic effects compared to Methimazole. Methimazole is effective but is associated with a higher risk of congenital malformations, making it less suitable for use in early pregnancy. Carbimazole, being a pro-drug of Methimazole, carries similar risks and is also not recommended in the first trimester. Perchlorate is not commonly used for hyperthyroidism treatment and lacks sufficient safety data in pregnancy, thus it is not a first-line option. Therefore, the consensus supports the use of Propylthiouracil as the safest choice for treating hyperthyroidism in the first trimester.
